newsitem.title: USA: Supreme Court won't lift FCC phone rule stay.
newsitem.headline: Supreme Court won't lift FCC phone rule stay.

text.p: The Supreme Court Tuesday declined a request by federal regulators to reactivate landmark rules intended to pry open the nation's local phone monopolies to competition.

The action means that, for now, the deregulation of the $100 billion local phone market will depend largely on individual rulings by state regulators -- instead of uniform rules set by the Federal Communications Commission.

It is a defeat for the FCC and long-distance companies such as AT&T Corp. and MCI Communications Corp. They asked the high court to reinstate the rules after a U.S. appeals court in St. Louis last month suspended key parts until it rules on a challenge to the measure. At the end of October, Justice Clarence Thomas refused to lift the lower court's "stay."
It is a victory for the Baby Bell phone companies, other local carriers and state regulators seeking to overturn the FCC's "interconnection" rules in the St. Louis court.
The high court made its action known in a one-sentence statement that gave no explanation for the move.

The FCC rules detail how long-distance carriers, cable-TV operators, utilities and others wanting to offer local phone service can link up to the local phone network under the new telecommunications law.

Thomas oversees appeals from the St. Louis-based appeals court. After he declined to reinstate the rules, the FCC and its long-distance allies asked Justices Ruth Bader Ginsberg and John Paul Stevens, respectively, to reconsider the request. The justices referred the matter to the entire court.
